parameters.query:
-- Claim approved messages for sending, and move each one to 'queued' in the
-- same statement so a second run cannot take it.
--
-- Every guard docs/workflows.md lists is here, in the order it lists them.
-- They are in the claim rather than in a later IF node on purpose: a guard
-- that runs after the row has been picked up can only refuse to send it,
-- which leaves the row claimed and needing a human. A guard in the WHERE
-- clause never claims it at all.
--
-- OUTREACH_PAUSED is first because it is the stop button. When it is true
-- this statement returns zero rows and nothing downstream executes at all,
-- whatever the other guards would have said.
WITH cfg AS (
    SELECT $1::jsonb AS p
),
local AS (
    -- Evaluated in the configured timezone, not the server's. A message that
    -- arrives at 03:00 local time reads as automation no matter how well it
    -- is written.
    SELECT now() AT TIME ZONE (SELECT p ->> 'timezone' FROM cfg) AS ts
),
gate AS (
    SELECT
        NOT (SELECT (p ->> 'paused')::boolean FROM cfg) AS not_paused,
        EXTRACT(isodow FROM (SELECT ts FROM local))::int IN (
            SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(p -> 'working_days')::int FROM cfg
        ) AS in_working_days,
        EXTRACT(hour FROM (SELECT ts FROM local))::int
            >= (SELECT (p ->> 'hour_start')::int FROM cfg)
        AND EXTRACT(hour FROM (SELECT ts FROM local))::int
            <  (SELECT (p ->> 'hour_end')::int FROM cfg) AS in_working_hours
),
spent_today AS (
    -- What already counts against today's allowance. 'queued' counts as well
    -- as 'sent': a row in flight is going to become sent, and counting it only
    -- once it has would overshoot the daily limit by a whole batch every run.
    SELECT count(*)::int AS n
    FROM outreach o
    WHERE o.status IN ('sent', 'queued')
      AND COALESCE(o.sent_at, o.updated_at)
              AT TIME ZONE (SELECT p ->> 'timezone' FROM cfg)
          >= date_trunc('day', (SELECT ts FROM local))
),
allowance AS (
    SELECT GREATEST(
        (SELECT (p ->> 'daily_limit')::int FROM cfg) - (SELECT n FROM spent_today),
        0
    ) AS n
),
locked AS (
    -- A pool rather than exactly what will be sent, because the per-domain
    -- rule below has to choose between siblings and cannot do that if they
    -- were never locked. Locks release at the end of this statement either
    -- way, so over-locking costs nothing.
    SELECT o.id, o.created_at, c.domain, l.score
    FROM outreach o
    JOIN leads     l  ON l.id  = o.lead_id
    JOIN people    pe ON pe.id = l.person_id
    JOIN companies c  ON c.id  = l.company_id
    WHERE o.status = 'approved'
      AND (SELECT not_paused AND in_working_days AND in_working_hours FROM gate)
      AND (SELECT n FROM allowance) > 0
      -- The recipient must still be reachable. The trigger on outreach refuses
      -- a suppressed address anyway, but a transaction that aborts at send
      -- time has already spent the claim; refusing here costs nothing.
      AND pe.email IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT is_suppressed(pe.email)
      -- Per-domain ceiling for today, counting the same two statuses as above.
      AND (
          SELECT count(*)
          FROM outreach o2
          JOIN leads     l2 ON l2.id = o2.lead_id
          JOIN companies c2 ON c2.id = l2.company_id
          WHERE c2.domain = c.domain
            AND o2.status IN ('sent', 'queued')
            AND COALESCE(o2.sent_at, o2.updated_at)
                    AT TIME ZONE (SELECT p ->> 'timezone' FROM cfg)
                >= date_trunc('day', (SELECT ts FROM local))
      ) < (SELECT (p ->> 'per_domain_limit')::int FROM cfg)
    ORDER BY l.score DESC NULLS LAST, o.created_at
    LIMIT (SELECT (p ->> 'batch_size')::int * 4 FROM cfg)
    FOR UPDATE OF o SKIP LOCKED
),
one_per_domain AS (
    -- The subquery above cannot see a sibling claimed in this same run, so two
    -- messages to the same company would both pass it. At most one row per
    -- domain per run closes that, and is exactly right at the default limit of
    -- one. Above that it under-sends and the next run catches up, which is the
    -- side to err on.
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (domain) id, domain, score, created_at
    FROM locked
    ORDER BY domain, score DESC NULLS LAST, created_at
),
chosen AS (
    SELECT id FROM one_per_domain
    ORDER BY score DESC NULLS LAST, created_at
    LIMIT LEAST((SELECT (p ->> 'batch_size')::int FROM cfg), (SELECT n FROM allowance))
),
queued AS (
    UPDATE outreach
    SET status = 'queued'
    WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM chosen)
      AND status = 'approved'
    RETURNING id
)
SELECT q.id            AS outreach_id,
       o.lead_id,
       o.subject,
       o.body,
       o.sequence_step,
       pe.email        AS recipient_email,
       pe.full_name    AS recipient_name,
       c.id            AS company_id,
       c.name          AS company_name,
       c.domain
FROM queued q
JOIN outreach  o  ON o.id  = q.id
JOIN leads     l  ON l.id  = o.lead_id
JOIN people    pe ON pe.id = l.person_id
JOIN companies c  ON c.id  = l.company_id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ paused: String($env.OUTREACH_PAUSED ?? 'true').toLowerCase() !== 'false', daily_limit: Number($env.OUTREACH_DAILY_LIMIT || 5), per_domain_limit: Number($env.OUTREACH_PER_DOMAIN_LIMIT || 1), batch_size: Number($env.OUTREACH_DISPATCH_BATCH_SIZE || 5), hour_start: Number($env.OUTREACH_WORKING_HOUR_START || 9), hour_end: Number($env.OUTREACH_WORKING_HOUR_END || 17), working_days: String($env.OUTREACH_WORKING_DAYS || '1,2,3,4,5').split(',').map(s => Number(s.trim())).filter(n => n >= 1 && n <= 7), timezone: $env.GENERIC_TIMEZONE || 'UTC' } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- The message left the building. Record it once, in one transaction: the
-- outreach row, the conversation the reply will arrive on, the outbound
-- message itself, and the lead.
--
-- Every write is guarded on the state the claim left behind, so replaying this
-- statement cannot send a second message or double-write a thread.
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j),
sent AS (
    UPDATE outreach o
    SET status              = 'sent',
        sent_at             = now(),
        provider_message_id = p.j ->> 'message_id',
        error               = NULL
    FROM p
    WHERE o.id = (p.j ->> 'outreach_id')::uuid
      AND o.status = 'queued'
    RETURNING o.id, o.lead_id, o.subject, o.body
),
conv AS (
    -- The thread key is the Message-ID the provider reported. WF-08 matches a
    -- reply back to this row, so a send that produced no id is not threadable
    -- and the COALESCE below keeps it unique rather than colliding on ''.
    INSERT INTO conversations (lead_id, channel, external_thread_id, status, last_message_at)
    SELECT sent.lead_id, 'email',
           COALESCE(NULLIF(p.j ->> 'message_id', ''), 'outreach:' || sent.id::text),
           'awaiting_reply', now()
    FROM sent, p
    ON CONFLICT (channel, external_thread_id) DO UPDATE
        SET last_message_at = now()
    RETURNING id, lead_id
),
msg AS (
    INSERT INTO messages (conversation_id, direction, author, subject, body,
                          external_message_id, sent_at)
    SELECT conv.id, 'outbound', 'agent', sent.subject, sent.body,
           NULLIF(p.j ->> 'message_id', ''), now()
    FROM conv, sent, p
    ON CONFLICT (external_message_id) WHERE external_message_id IS NOT NULL
        DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id
),
lead AS (
    UPDATE leads
    SET status = 'contacted'
    WHERE id = (SELECT lead_id FROM sent)
      AND status IN ('pending_approval', 'approved', 'queued')
    RETURNING id
)
SELECT (SELECT id FROM sent)                 AS outreach_id,
       (SELECT id FROM conv)                 AS conversation_id,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM msg)::int       AS messages_written,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM lead)::int      AS leads_contacted,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'message_id'            AS provider_message_id,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'recipient_email'       AS recipient_email,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'company_name'          AS company_name;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ outreach_id: $('Claim Approved Outreach').item.json.outreach_id, recipient_email: $('Claim Approved Outreach').item.json.recipient_email, company_name: $('Claim Approved Outreach').item.json.company_name, message_id: ($json.messageId || '') } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- The provider refused it. Park the row at 'failed' with the reason and tell
-- a human; do not retry.
--
-- docs/workflows.md: "A send error sets failed with the error text and does not
-- retry automatically." An automatic retry against an unknown error is how one
-- rejected message becomes four delivered ones, because an SMTP error can
-- arrive after the message was in fact accepted.
--
-- The lead is deliberately not touched. The claim moved the outreach row and
-- nothing else, so the lead is still where the approval left it.
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j),
failed AS (
    UPDATE outreach o
    SET status = 'failed',
        error  = left(COALESCE(NULLIF(p.j ->> 'error', ''), 'unknown send error'), 2000)
    FROM p
    WHERE o.id = (p.j ->> 'outreach_id')::uuid
      AND o.status = 'queued'
    RETURNING o.id, o.lead_id
),
alert AS (
    -- LATERAL so that nothing is queued when the UPDATE matched nothing:
    -- a dedup_key built from an absent id would be one shared key for every
    -- such case, which is the opposite of deduplication.
    SELECT q.*
    FROM failed
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL queue_notification(
        'system',
        'system:send_failed:' || failed.id::text,
        'Send failed: ' || COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'company_name', ''), 'unknown'),
        'Recipient: ' || COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'recipient_email', ''), 'unknown')
            || E'\n' || 'Outreach: ' || failed.id::text
            || E'\n\n' || left(COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'error', ''), 'unknown send error'), 900)
            || E'\n\n' || 'The message stays at failed and is not retried. '
            || 'Inspect it before approving anything else.',
        'immediate',
        jsonb_build_object('outreach_id', failed.id, 'kind', 'send_failure'),
        NULL::uuid,
        failed.lead_id,
        interval '1 hour'
    ) q
)
SELECT (SELECT id FROM failed)                       AS outreach_id,
       (SELECT notification_id FROM alert)           AS notification_id,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'company_name'                  AS company_name,
       left(COALESCE($1::jsonb ->> 'error', ''), 300) AS error;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ outreach_id: $('Claim Approved Outreach').item.json.outreach_id, recipient_email: $('Claim Approved Outreach').item.json.recipient_email, company_name: $('Claim Approved Outreach').item.json.company_name, error: ($json.error?.message || $json.error || 'unknown send error') } ) }}
